question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

decoded.challenge: www-authenticate: Bearer, with two parameters, resource_metadata="https://mcp.ashbyhq.com/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource" and scope="openid mcp offline_access" (kept here rather than under headers, and with a comma inserted after Bearer, because the schema's credential rule reads a long token-alphabet run after Bearer as a token; the transcript carries the header as received)
decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; resource https://mcp.ashbyhq.com/mcp/v1; authorization_servers: https://mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/oidc; scopes_supported: openid, mcp, offline_access; bearer_methods_supported: header
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server/oidc; issuer https://mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/oidc; registration_endpoint present (/oidc/reg); the same three scopes; PKCE S256; grants implicit, authorization_code, refresh_token; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_jwt, client_secret_post, private_key_jwt, none
decoded.rest: GET https://api.ashbyhq.com/candidate.list with no Authorization header answers 401 with an empty text/plain body and no www-authenticate (the vendor documents this API as POST with Basic auth; a GET was sent because the probe script makes one keyless GET)

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.ashbyhq.com/mcp/v1 answers 401 with a Bearer challenge naming its protected-resource metadata and the scope it wants (openid mcp offline_access), and a one-word JSON error. The metadata names a dedicated OIDC issuer, mcp-auth.ashbyhq.com/oidc, with the same three scopes. That server advertises dynamic registration, PKCE S256, five token-auth methods including none, and three grants of which one is implicit, the grant OAuth 2.1 removes; whether the MCP flow can use it is not something this probe measures. A keyless GET on the REST API answers 401 with an empty body and no challenge. Same challenge as the 2026-09-13 measurement in the entry's notes; the issuer and the grant list are recorded here for the first time. Nothing here measures what either server does with a credential.
